fixes.fix: Explained "All contemporary 48 states were part of the _____ United States presidential election"
fixes.text:
VERDICT: 1916
WHY: The 1916 presidential election was the first in which all 48 contemporary contiguous states participated, following the admission of Arizona and New Mexico in 1912.
TRAPS: Do not confuse with 1912 (only 46 states) or 1920 (still 48 but later). The phrase "contemporary 48 states" refers to the Union's composition at that time.
HOOK: Memory hook — "1916: 48 stars finally align." Exam-day trap — never assume 1912 had 48 states; it had 46.

fixes.fix: Explained "Florida voters chose six electors to the _____, which selected the President and Vice Pres"
fixes.text:
VERDICT: The blank is "Electoral College".
WHY: The US President and Vice President are elected indirectly by electors chosen by each state; Florida's six electors (based on its congressional delegation) cast votes in the Electoral College.
TRAPS: Don't confuse with "Congress" (which counts votes but doesn't elect), "Senate" (only breaks VP ties), or "popular vote" (doesn't directly decide).
